text:
jordan: hey everyone, jordan here (started today). trying to get set up for a quick spike that needs a staging DB user + access to the KMS key for encrypting test blobs. who should I ping and what's the fastest path? :wave:
rachel: welcome! add me and @tom (your buddy) to the request. for staging we usually do a short-lived Vault credential or a service account with 24h token.
tom: hi jordan — quick path: open the secrets portal and pick 'temporary dev creds'. the portal will create a Vault dynamic user and attach a policy scoped to the staging DB. SLA is usually a few hours during business hours.
jordan: where's the portal? and what info do they need exactly?
devex-bot: devex resources -> https://internal.redwood/tools/secrets-request. Template fields: service, owner, env, resource path, access (roles), justification, expires_at.
ops: addendum from ops: for KMS access include the key resource name and the exact operation (encrypt/decrypt). we grant encrypt-only to dev spikes unless you need decrypt. please don't request unrestricted key access.
jordan: example values ok?
ops: yes, paste this snippet into the portal to save time:
```
service: jordan-spike
owner: jordan@redwood.com
env: staging
resource: projects/redwood-staging/sql/instance-7/databases/feature_x
access: role=feature_spike_reader, operations=db-connect
kms: projects/redwood-staging/locations/global/keyRings/spike/cryptoKeys/staging-encrypt
reason: quick perf spike for cache tuning; access expires in 48h
```
rachel: also include that you want a time-limited token (24-48h). if you need extension, file another request and include justification. production keys will need eng-security approval and longer lead times.
eng-security: quick note — prod KMS and prod DB access require ticket + manager approval + 2fa confirmation. For dev/staging we allow scoped ephemeral creds. We monitor key usage and will revoke if suspicious.
jordan: do I need to add rotation ownership for staging?
tom: not for ephemeral. if they give static creds (rare), put rotation owner and cadence. default policy: static secrets must have owner and rotation <= 90d.
jordan: what's the Vault path I'll use once approved?
ops: you'll get a message with the Vault path, usually secret/data/dynamic/jordan-spike or secret/data/services/feature_x/staging. commands we use: ```vault login -method=oidc role=redwood-dev && vault read secret/data/dynamic/jordan-spike```
jordan: sweet. will this show the password in plaintext?
ops: Vault returns the secret JSON; clients should use the SDK or env var injection. try to avoid printing creds in logs.
rachel: final checklist for you before opening request: 1) paste snippet, 2) tag me and @tom, 3) set expires_at, 4) indicate if you need decrypt rights on KMS.
jordan: opening request now. thanks all! :tada:
devex-bot: automated reply — request created: SR-9987. Expect staging access within 4h during business hours. If no action in 24h, this thread will be escalated.
eng-security: FYI @rachel — we'll be copied on the prod route; not needed for this staging request.
jordan: got the approval email and vault path, thanks everyone. one more q — how do I rotate locally cached creds?
tom: kill the token and request a new one via the portal or run `vault token revoke <token>`; local SDK caches may need restart. simple approach: `pkill -f dev-server` and relogin.
jordan: awesome, closing this thread once I finish the spike. thanks again! :thumbsup:
